label: rem:quantum-ideal-gas-law-interpretation
title: Noether invariant and comparison with classical $PV = NkT$
html:
Remark. Noether invariant and comparison with classical PV = NkT

Noether invariant. The quantum ideal gas law manifests identically as the Ward identity of a scale symmetry of the partition function. Under the q-deformed Noether dictionary, the strictly conserved quantity under simultaneous rescaling of V_q and \beta_q is the quantum free energy F_q.

We define the thermodynamic Noether current:

  \mathcal{J}_q^{\mathrm{thermo}} = V_q \,\frac{\partial}{\partial V_q} + \beta_q \,\frac{\partial}{\partial \beta_q}.

The identity \mathcal{J}_q^{\mathrm{thermo}}(\ln Z_q) = 0 holds strictly at the equation-of-state surface. The quantum ideal gas law P_q V_q = N T_q (1 + \cdots) is exactly the content of this vanishing. It structurally parallels the classical Euler relation E = TS - PV + \mu N.

Comparison with the classical derivation. See Table.

Classical limit. As q \to 1, T_q = \hbar_q \to 0. However, N T_q = N \hbar_q remains finite in physical units via k_B. The correction vanishes identically as \hbar_q^2 \to 0. We recover the classical ideal gas law PV = Nk_BT.
